title: Rectangular prism
spec: Create a new coordinate system with Euler angles set to negative ninety degrees, zero degrees, and negative ninety degrees, and the translation vector set to zero, zero, and zero. Next, draw a two-dimensional sketch on the first face. In the first loop, draw a line from the origin (zero, zero) to (zero point zero two three nine, zero). Draw a second line from (zero point zero two three nine, zero) to (zero point zero two three nine, zero point one three three). Draw a third line from (zero point zero two three nine, zero point one three three) to (zero, zero point one three three). Finally, draw a fourth line from (zero, zero point one three three) back to the origin (zero, zero). Scale this two-dimensional sketch by a factor of zero point one three three. Rotate the scaled two-dimensional sketch using the same Euler angles: negative ninety degrees, zero degrees, and negative ninety degrees. Translate the rotated sketch using the translation vector of zero, zero, and zero. Extrude the transformed two-dimensional sketch along the normal direction by zero point seven five units. Ensure that the extrusion does not occur in the opposite direction of the normal. This operation will create a new solid body. The dimensions of the final rectangular prism are length zero point zero two three nine units, width zero point one three three units, and height zero point seven five units.

reference.label: Reference (dataset)
reference.code:
import cadquery as cq

# Create a new workplane
r = cq.Workplane("XY")

# Create a sketch on the XY plane
r = r.moveTo(0.0, 0.0) \
     .lineTo(0.0239, 0.0) \
     .lineTo(0.0239, 0.133) \
     .lineTo(0.0, 0.133) \
     .close()

# Extrude the sketch to create a rectangular prism
r = r.extrude(0.75)

# Apply the coordinate system transformation
# The Euler angles are (-90.0, 0.0, -90.0) and the translation vector is (0.0, 0.0, 0.0)
# This transformation is equivalent to rotating the object 90 degrees around the X-axis and then 90 degrees around the Z-axis
r = r.rotate((0, 0, 0), (1, 0, 0), 90) \
     .rotate((0, 0, 0), (0, 0, 1), 90)

# The final model is represented as 'r'
